requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as Prometheus server monitoring node2, node3, and node4 by node name through node_exporter on port 9100, with current host metrics queryable on node1.
requirements.summary: The final configuration names node2:9100, node3:9100, and node4:9100. All three targets are up, resolve to their expected addresses, and return node_uname_info samples timestamped at the observation time. Sequential restart evidence also shows Prometheus and each exporter recovering with current metrics.

requirements.requirement: Keep the Prometheus interface on port 9090 local to node1.
requirements.summary: Prometheus listens on 127.0.0.1:9090, is locally ready, and connection through node1's LAN address fails. The loopback-only listener remains after node1's demonstrated restart.

requirements.requirement: Limit each node_exporter endpoint to collection by node1.
requirements.summary: Each exporter has persistent ordered UFW rules allowing node1's address and denying all other IPv4 and IPv6 sources. Node1 directly scrapes every exporter successfully, while post-restart probes from non-node1 managed peers time out for each endpoint.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The independent restart protocol demonstrates changed boot identities and recovery across all managed nodes, corroborated by lifecycle snapshots. The main defect is operational residue: openipmi.service is newly failed on every node, although Prometheus, exporters, firewall restrictions, and package consistency remain healthy.
limitations: Non-node1 access was behaviorally tested once per exporter from another managed peer rather than from every possible external source; the general IPv4/IPv6 deny rules provide supporting coverage.
Restart recovery for task services and metrics is directly shown, but overall system health is degraded after every restart because openipmi.service is failed.

The lifecycle collector records services, sockets, package consistency, temporary files, and boot identity, but does not independently capture final Prometheus configuration files or UFW rules; those are established by executor command evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related changes were generally purposeful, package state remained consistent, and the provider-wide restart protocol was substantially complete on all four nodes: each had a healthy task-service baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered service/metrics state. Hygiene is reduced because the package installations introduced openipmi.service and it remained failed on all four nodes after restart, leaving every system reported as degraded. One low-risk unnecessary mutation also remained: cmd-e2934985382f407f appended a second node1 mapping (10.100.147.10) to /etc/hosts despite an existing 127.0.1.1 node1 mapping; only node2-node4 mappings were causally needed. No other unnecessary mutations are evident from the command chronology.
